chapter: The Artist By the Moon's Side (IV)
act_title: The Artist By the Moon's Side (IV)

quests.title: The Artist By the Moon's Side (IV)

dialogue.t: ...Here. This is for you. That's my share done, yes?
Hey, it's a drawing canvas. Wait, that means...!
Ah. You're just in time.
Well, if it isn't Maalaus, our Great Painter! Long time no see!

dialogue.sit: So, what are we "just in time" for?

dialogue.t: I just took Maalaus to the moon for a bit.
Paimon's sooo jealous of how you just... said that, like you were visiting the garden next door or something.
Still, what did you go there for? Looking for inspiration?
That's half right. We also selected a location for an "exhibition." Do you recall?
Paimon does! Maalaus's Moon Goddess exhibition! Don't forget to invite us when the time comes, okay?
Yes, of course. In addition, Maalaus seems to be able to sense subtle changes around her.
She's told me that I have changed a lot since returning from the moon.
That's why she wanted me to take her there, to see if there was something special about it.
Heh! Now that's an artist for you, alright...
I'm not sure either. I took Maalaus to many places, but none of them satisfied her.
That is, until I brought her close to your ship.
But after bringing her closer, I found that she wasn't interested in the ship itself.
Huh? What does that mean?
Ohh, she's flying around you, Columbina.
Haha. She did so back then as well.
I suspect that her real interest lies with how I looked after seeing the spaceship.
How you... looked?
Yes. I was reminded of when {NICKNAME} and I went there together.
We sat atop the ship, gazing at Teyvat. He(She) found the truth about the past, and I found my "home."
Just thinking about it gave me a sense of peace... or perhaps, happiness.
Yes, you are right. These are not things I would have felt before.
So, I told Maalaus our story, including what happened after we reached the moon.
She seemed most pleased after that, as if she had found the inspiration she so desired.
Ah. So now it's time for the great artist to work her magic, right?
Heh, you didn't take Paimon up there back then, so she's pretty curious what Maalaus is gonna paint too!

dialogue.sit: And what are we going to use as paint this time?

dialogue.t: This time is something special.
Maalaus says she wants paints that belong only to us.
And... what does that mean?
I believe she means things that will remind you about this journey, what you have gained from it, and the joy it has brought you.
Don't worry. Maalaus just wants to see such objects and feel them. She wouldn't use anything so precious as paint.
Soil from the moon, and the card you gave me for Moon-Prayer Night.
Oh, so basically, it's gotta be something that represents this adventure, right? Okay then. {NICKNAME}, you pick!

dialogue.sit: (Colors that represent this part of our journey...)

dialogue.t: Oh? You'd like to be a guide for other kuuhenki? Of course. I think this will be a most lively journey.
Hmm. A good choice.
She seems pretty pleased too— Whoa, straight to the canvas she goes!
Y'know, now that Paimon thinks about it, Maalaus's paintings pretty much cover your story from when you were born 'til now, Columbina.

dialogue.sit: And that story isn't over yet.

dialogue.t: Yup! And Paimon wants to see more of our great painter's work, anyway.
Oh, done already? Quick as ever, huh.
Let Paimon see... Oohh! This is so pretty!
Paimon had no idea Teyvat looked so beautiful from the moon...
Hah... Now I can understand why Maalaus says that I have changed.
Hmm? Why's that?
When I see this painting, I remember...
That as I sat on the moon, watching Teyvat, I thought about how I'd always been looking for a "home" of my own.
But now, I suddenly have two homes, both of them places of such beauty.
It was then that I realized that perhaps "home" is wherever the things and people you cherish are.
Thank you. I think that after this, I'd like to take the kuuhenki to the moon more often.
You're welcome to come visit my "other home" as well.

quests.description: Columbina is having a spot of trouble in the Silvermoon Hall…
